60.7% (230 vs 234 bytes). Same algorithm (axis from two nodes' world positions in a frame, _finite guard); retail keeps y in a stack slot where VC6 keeps it in a register, so register allocation and FPU ordering diverge.

text .VUE loader, lines 0x1c9/0x1ec/0x1f9/0x22a. 48%: identical structure and calls, but register allocation is permuted (retail ebx/ebp and esi/edi swapped relative to ours), which shifts most ModRM bytes
cdecl; slot 7 helper. 90.66%: the two Vec3Normalize result temporaries sit at a different stack slot (retail esp+0x70/0x7c, ours reuses the axisX/position slot) and one fld is scheduled earlier

cdecl; slot 7 helper. ~56% (was ~27% before UnitVector named its inverse length): same control flow and layout, but VC6 inlines differently: retail calls Vec3::Vec3 for the identity axis and, in the axisY path, calls DotProduct and inlines operator* (calling Vec3::Vec3); ours inlines the ctor and DotProduct and calls operator*. Every later byte shifts
cdecl; slot 7 / 0x4a9050 helper. ~19%. Same calls in the same order except that VC6 inlines the first CrossProduct (retail calls 0x00515600 twice), which shifts every later byte (inline budget)

ret 0xc; slot 7, playback of a non-looping motion with interpolation/extrapolation and blending. 3330 vs 3327 bytes with the same call sequence (AdvanceClamped x2, the operator COMDATs, PoseRotation/RotatePose x2, InterpolatePose x3, BlendToMotion) and the retail smoothstep/clamp shape, but VC6 calls CharacterPose::CharacterPose (0x4a8930) three times then twice where retail calls it twice then four times, inlines the extrapolation operators retail calls (retail only inlines operator- there and calls Vec3::Vec3), and allocates the frame differently (0x284 vs 0x2dc); every byte after the first expansion shifts; 4.79% relocation-masked
